title: Why one viral story feels like EVERYONE

voice.tone: calm-smart friend who catches you mid-spiral
voice.style: short punch lines; name the bias once; one everyday mirror; never clinical lecture

slides.headline: MYTH
slides.body: If it's everywhere in my feed… it's happening to everyone.

slides.headline: Sounds right. Brains love loud.
slides.body: One dramatic story sticks. Quiet base rates don't. So your brain upgrades "I saw it" into "it's everywhere."

slides.headline: FACT · availability cascade
slides.body: Repeat a vivid claim → it feels common → people talk → it feels even more common. Frequency in attention ≠ frequency in reality.

slides.headline: Catch it today
slides.body: Exam rumor: three group chats panic. Base rate? Still one quiz, same week, same curve. Drama traveled. Numbers didn't.

slides.headline: Which myth next?
slides.body: Save this. Comment the bias you catch yourself using this week.
